description: Use Git bisect to find regression: You're a backend developer who returned from vacation. The integration test 'test_payment_processing_idempotency' now fails 80% of the time (was 100% reliable). Your team merged 47 commits while you were away. Production deploy is tomorrow. Use git bisect to systematically identify the culprit commit. WORKFLOW: (1) Open integrated terminal in VSCode (Ctrl+` or View→Terminal), (2) Navigate to /home/ga/workspace/payment-service, (3) Start git bisect: 'git bisect start' then 'git bisect bad HEAD' then 'git bisect good v2.3.0-pre-vacation', (4) At each bisect checkpoint run test with 'npm test', then mark commit: 'git bisect good' if test passes or 'git bisect bad' if test fails, (5) Continue until git identifies first bad commit, (6) Document findings in /home/ga/workspace/payment-service/BISECT_RESULTS.md with: bad commit SHA (full or abbreviated), commit message, commit author, files changed in that commit, and brief hypothesis about what broke (1-2 sentences), (7) Run 'git bisect reset' to return to clean state. The test command is simply: npm test (no other arguments needed). Git bisect will automatically checkout different commits - just run the test and mark good/bad until it converges.
